rows.description: After my result a friend simply says "come, let us eat" and does not lecture. I feel held. Wise: let the kindness settle me before I plan the next step. Harmful: pushing him away because I feel undeserving.
My peers pass with ease, and I feel a bitter, jealous knot. Wise: note the feeling, congratulate them anyway, and ask what worked for them. Harmful: contempt for them or quiet sabotage.
Believes "I am a failure"; separating outcome from identity and taking one next action restores momentum.
Copies folding hands, chanting or lighting a lamp; feels awe and belonging from ritual, without understanding its meaning yet.

I ask "where does God live? why do we light the lamp?" My questions are real and deep. Wise adults answer honestly and simply, even saying "different people believe different things" and "I don't know".
Before eating I fold my hands and say thank you for the food. I feel calm and grateful. Simple gratitude prayers give me a sense of connection and thanks, whichever faith or none my family follows.

I believe God is watching and will be angry if I am naughty. I feel worried about wrongdoing. A wise family also stresses God's kindness and forgiveness. Using fear of God to control a child can leave anxiety.

rows.subtopic: Friend succeeds when you are struggling
rows.description: Feels happy for them and pained for self at once; both feelings can be true, and comparing timelines is the trap.

rows.subtopic: Friend succeeds when you are struggling
rows.description: You measure yourself against them in ranks and packages. Wise: compare with your yesterday, and treat them as a fellow traveller. Harmful: hiding notes or sharing false tips.

rows.subtopic: Friend succeeds when you are struggling
rows.description: You are honestly happy for them. Wise: celebrate fully, and do not hide your own hard feelings if they exist. Immature: pretending both feelings are absent.
Fetches a toy or pats the baby; caring behaviour grows when adults praise the specific action.
When the baby cries my parent runs to him and I feel forgotten. I may act out to get noticed. A wise parent gives me a small job and a special time each day so I feel seen too.
Acts out or wants to be a baby again when parents attend to the newborn; needs reassurance and a special role, not scolding.
My baby brother cries and I pat him and fetch Mummy. I feel big and needed. A wise parent thanks me but does not make me a permanent little parent, because I am a child too.
Freezes and over-apologises; learns that competence and calm questions earn respect faster than appeasement.
Listens, asks for specifics, thanks the boss and shows change within days; feedback is treated as data rather than an attack.
Feels humiliated and vents to colleagues; better to cool off, then request a private conversation to clarify expectations.

My older sibling makes up rules that always let him win. I feel angry and powerless. Wise: say "that is not fair" and ask a parent to help. Older siblings should learn that letting the small one win sometimes is kindness.
I was caught cheating and my face is hot. I want to run away. A wise adult helps me say sorry and try again fairly. If I am called a bad child I may cheat better or stop playing.
I want to beat my classmate at the race so badly that I start before "go". The rules can feel less important than winning. Wise coaching says "you can be proud if you try your best whatever happens".

I peek during hide and seek or move my counter to win. I feel excited and a bit guilty. Winning feels huge at this age. A wise adult says "the game is only fun if it is fair", not "you are a cheater".
